statement: One line holds a non-negative integer n. Print yes when n reads the same forwards and backwards, and no otherwise. The arithmetic route: build the full reversal with the digit loop, then compare it to the original - which means the original must be saved before the loop, because the loop consumes its working copy down to 0. Negative signs never appear here, but trailing zeros matter: any number ending in 0 (except 0 itself) cannot be a palindrome, since no number starts with 0.
constraints: Input has no sign and no leading zeros.

example.why: The reversal of 121 is 121 - the digits mirror around the centre 2.

hint: Two variables: the untouched original and the working copy the loop destroys.
mistake: Comparing the reversal against the loop variable after the loop - that variable is 0 by then.
